Components / Forms

Text area

.dr-field--area · --area6 · --half · .dr-field__input · .dr-field__label · .dr-field__hint · components/form.css · kit specimen

Anatomy

1–2 lines clients see. Your experience and the area you cover.
  1. 1.dr-field--areaThe row, stacked: min-height 80, padding 12 top and bottom. It stays out of the group's label grid.
  2. 2.dr-field__labelThe question, on its own line above the box. Where the screen title already asks it, the label is visually hidden instead.
  3. 3.dr-field__inputThe box: --media at radius 10 with a 12px inset. Typed --ink 13.33:1, placeholder --slate 5.51:1. No resize handle and no focus ring; the caret carries the focus.
  4. 4.dr-field__hintThe format, by example, under the box.

Variants and sizes

Inventory rows: Form field (multiline).

When to use

A text area collects prose the user writes in their own words: a message to support, notes for the operator, the description of an issue, a review. Its height is the promise. It tells the user how much to write before they start, so the modifier is chosen by what the screen is asking for, not by the space left over. It stands on contact-support, order-setup, report-issue, rate and operator-profile-setup.

The placeholder shows a real example of an answer, never a restatement of the label: Floor, entrance code, what's inside… under Notes for the operator. What the user types is theirs and is not rewritten.

Sources: DESIGN.md § Text areas, and the focus rule they changed · voice.md § Microcopy — rules by element type (hint) · microcopy.md § USER · inventory.md § 1.5

Rule and anti-rule

Do

report-issue's description: a drawn question, six lines of room, and a placeholder that shows the kind of detail that settles a claim.

Don’t

Six lines for a one-line value. A short typed value belongs in a field, and a value chosen from a set in a picker row. An oversized box promises an answer the screen does not want.
